target.title: security(audit): flag control-plane exposure and plugin command surfaces
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes two related gaps in `openclaw security audit` where operators could miss high-impact exposure on open chat surfaces and extension plugin command entry points.

### Gap 1: Control-plane tools on open inbound policy

When a channel uses `groupPolicy="open"` or an open DM policy, the exposure matrix flagged elevated and runtime/filesystem tools but did **not** separately flag **control-plane tools** (`cron`, `gateway`).

### Gap 2: Extension plugin command reachability

Native/plugin command entry points that bypass the LLM were not surfaced distinctly when auditing installed plugins and channel command surfaces.

**Concrete example:** WhatsApp `groupPolicy: "open"` with `tools.profile: "coding"` exposes cron/gateway control-plane tools to any group member, and enabled extensions without `plugins.allow` can expose plugin commands that bypass the LLM — neither was called out distinctly before this PR.

## Why This Change Was Made

Extends trust-model and plugin-trust audit collectors so open inbound policies with reachable control-plane tools and LLM-bypass plugin commands emit dedicated findings with explicit detail strings.

## User Impact

**Before:** Operators could miss automation/gateway control exposure and plugin command surfaces on open channels.

**After:** Audit emits `security.exposure.open_groups_with_control_plane` (critical) and `plugins.commands_reachable_chat_surface` / related plugin-trust findings with actionable detail.

## Evidence

- `src/security/audit-extra.sync.ts` — `collectExposureMatrixFindings` extensions for control-plane tools
- `src/security/audit-plugins-trust.ts` — plugin command reachability findings
- Diff: +287 / −67 across audit trust modules and docs

### Behavior proof

#### 1) Node runtime (`collectExposureMatrixFindings`, production export)

```text
=== #100945 audit control-plane exposure proof ===
Node: v22.22.0
open groupPolicy + coding profile findings:
  security.exposure.open_groups_with_runtime_or_fs (critical)
  security.exposure.open_groups_with_control_plane (critical)
flags control-plane: true
control-plane severity: critical
```

Config exercised: `{ channels: { whatsapp: { groupPolicy: "open" } }, tools: { elevated: { enabled: false }, profile: "coding" } }`

#### 2) Call-site regression tests (real Vitest stdout)

```text
$ pnpm test src/security/audit-plugins-trust.test.ts src/security/audit-trust-model.test.ts --reporter=verbose

 ✓ security audit trust model findings > evaluates trust-model exposure findings 4ms
 ✓ security audit install metadata findings > evaluates install metadata findings 214ms
 ✓ security audit extension tool reachability findings > evaluates extension tool reachability findings 19ms

 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  6 passed (6)
   Duration  772ms

[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 3.92s
```

Table-driven cases inside those suites include:

| Test case | Finding | Severity |
|-----------|---------|----------|
| `flags open groupPolicy when control-plane tools are exposed` | `security.exposure.open_groups_with_control_plane` | critical |
| `flags open groupPolicy when runtime/filesystem tools are exposed without guards` | `security.exposure.open_groups_with_runtime_or_fs` | critical |
| `flags enabled extensions when tool policy can expose plugin tools` | `plugins.commands_reachable_chat_surface` | warn |
| extension detail string | contains `plugin commands bypass the LLM` | — |

**Proof gap:** Full interactive `pnpm openclaw security audit` against a multi-channel production config was not run here; Node + Vitest drive the production audit collectors.
